content: Certain glucose-lowering medications exhibit direct protective effects on the kidneys that extend beyond their ability to control blood sugar levels. For example, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors decrease renal tubular glucose reabsorption, which leads to reductions in blood pressure and albuminuria. These effects collectively slow the rate of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) decline. Additionally, SGLT2 inhibitors mitigate oxidative stress and inflammation within kidney tissues, further contributing to renal protection. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists also provide protective effects for the kidneys. However, the renoprotective mechanisms of GLP-1 receptor agonists are not as extensively studied or understood compared to those of SGLT2 inhibitors. When selecting glucose-lowering therapies, it is essential to consider both cardiovascular and renal benefits, particularly in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD).
